os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session

stack_detection.method: bundle id; AX answers with full game state on first query
stack_detection.signature: com.apple.Chess; every piece an AXButton on first walk

t1_read_text.detail: Window title carries the live game state: 'Léandre Carpentier - Ordinateur (C'est aux blancs d'avancer)' — whose turn it is, as text.

t2_enumerate.detail: EVERY piece is an AXButton labeled with piece and square ('tour blanche, a1', 'pion blanc, d2'…) with its on-screen frame — the semantic view of a 3D-rendered game IS the game state. 72 nodes / 12.2 KB / 16 ms.

t4_living_screen.detail: Not tested (would require playing a move; read-only cell).

t5_blind_action.detail: Not exercised (a click would start moving pieces in a real game UI); frames are present and piece-precise, so aiming data exists.

t6_pictorial.detail: The 3D board region is fully COVERED by labeled piece buttons — no opaque gap to declare. The 'wanted negative' did not materialize on this app.

measurements.notes: This cell was planned as the perimeter-law negative (game = pixels-only) and REFUTED it for this app: Apple annotated its 3D game for VoiceOver, so the structured channel reads a chess position better than a vision model reads the same screenshot (piece-on-square, zero ambiguity, 3D perspective irrelevant). Honest scope note: Apple's own game is NOT representative of the game tier — unannotated GL/Metal surfaces (typical Steam titles) remain the expected pixels-only territory; the boundary is developer annotation effort, not app category.

runtime_verification.method: Board state from AX (16 white pieces on ranks 1–2, fresh game) vs the known just-launched state; title matches turn.
